text:
anya: FYI - HarborLine's LoRA merge into redwood-v2.1 produced shorter answers and a spike in EOS probability in early positions. I ran a tiny smoke set to confirm. Can infra/quant take a look?

matt: short answers how? give me the numbers or an example.

anya: Metrics from a 50-example customer smoke: top3_mass went 0.35 -> 0.51, avg entropy dropped 3.2 -> 2.6, median token length 20 -> 12. Example: prompt about billing -> base returned a 24-token explanation, merged returns a 6-token terse response ending with </s>.

zoe: did you apply the LoRA at runtime vs merging and compare? sometimes runtime application behaves differently.

anya: yes - runtime adapter path is fine; merging is where we see the problem. Merge command I used below.

```bash
# reproduce locally
python tools/merge_lora.py \
  --base models/redwood/v2.1 \
  --lora customer/harborline_lora.safetensors \
  --out /tmp/harbor-v2.1.merged.safetensors
# default merge currently folds to fp16
```

zoe: sounds like fp16 weight folding could be increasing softmax sharpness. Another possibility is accidental write to token embeddings or lm_head during merge.

leo: can you run a quick per-parameter mean-abs-diff between (base+runtime-adapter) and (base+merged) to see which modules diverge? I can help if you push diff script results.

anya: pasted the top diffs I saw from a lightweight diff tool (truncated names):

```
transformer.layers.6.mlp.fc_in.weight   mean-abs-diff 0.015  max 0.19
transformer.layers.11.attn.o_proj.weight mean-abs-diff 0.012 max 0.14
wte.weight (token embeddings)            mean-abs-diff 0.006 max 0.09
lm_head.weight                           mean-abs-diff 0.007 max 0.10
```

sam: token emb and lm_head showing non-zero drift is a red flag. Could be a sparse key collision in the LoRA checkpoint or a merge indexing bug. Did you verify tokenizer/vocab ids?

anya: I double-checked vocab size and special tokens, they match. Also reproduced one prompt where merged picks EOS at token 3 with prob 0.68 while runtime-adapter path spreads probability among common words.

matt: two-step plan: 1) re-run merge but preserve fp32 during fold, then quantize separately; 2) add a unit check in merge script to assert token-emb mean-diff < 0.02. If both pass, we can consider safe.

leo: queued a job to re-merge with --preserve-fp32 and then run our quantize script. Pls share the eval pack you used.

anya: eval pack command below and snippet of metrics file I produced.

```bash
python eval_pack/run_quick_eval.py \
  --model /tmp/harbor-v2.1.merged.safetensors \
  --prompt-set tests/customer_harbor_smoke.json \
  --out /tmp/harbor-eval.json
```

```json
# excerpt /tmp/harbor-eval.json
{
  "top3_mass": {"base": 0.35, "merged": 0.51},
  "entropy": {"base": 3.2, "merged": 2.6},
  "median_length": {"base": 20, "merged": 12}
}
```


eval-bot: job 1746123501 finished: merged(preserve-fp32)->quant->eval produced: top3_mass 0.39, entropy 3.0, median_length 17. Full log: https://internal/evals/1746123501

zoe: that's an improvement. Preserving fp32 during merge seems to mitigate most of the sharpness. We should still audit why token embeddings drifted at all.

matt: agreed. I'll run a per-layer correlation (pearson) between merged vs runtime-applied weights to produce a heatmap and capture top offenders. If we see token-emb changes > 0.02 mean-abs, flag as error.

sam: also recommend adding a minimal example diff file to onboarding deliverables (10 side-by-side prompts showing generated tokens + probs) so customers can sign off before we release merged artifacts to them.

anya: I'll prepare the 10-example mini-evalpack and share with HarborLine. ETA 90m.

leo: can we add to onboarding checklist: default merge uses --preserve-fp32, run post-quant eval, and run token-emb guard?

matt: yes. I'll open a PR to tools/merge_lora.py to change default and add the guard + an option to run quick eval as a post-merge smoke.

anya: thanks all. I'll drop artifacts and the customer diff into the ticket once ready.

zoe: nice find. marking this as "merge-behavior-investigation" in tracker.

anya: will update here after customer confirms. :white_check_mark:
